original.target_description: Rasinski et al. (2005), single reported study (assigned Study 1): University of Chicago undergraduates, honesty-related versus neutral vocabulary primes, one-way ANOVA on the summed zero-to-four index of four self-reported excessive alcohol-consumption behaviors, across both questionnaire orders.

n.sample_role: Undergraduate participants in the two-condition alcohol-behavior composite-index ANOVA.
n.exclusions: No exclusions are reported for this analysis; the stated 64 participants are corroborated by the reported F(1, 62) for the two-condition analysis.
n.location: Published p. 323, Method—Participants (PDF p. 3); p. 324, Results—Composite index (PDF p. 4)
n.quote: Sixty-four undergraduates were paid $3.00 to partic- … ipate in this study.

replication.target_description: Experiment 2: UCSD online adult panel participants; honesty versus neutral primes; mean proportion of four excessive-alcohol behavior questions endorsed; independent-groups t test.

n.quote: Data were obtained from 70 participants in the honesty condition and 82 participants in the neutral condition.
n.sample_role: Participants in the two-condition drinking-response test
n.exclusions: No exclusions in primary analysis; first 38 nonrandomly assigned participants retained. Separate 114-person sensitivity analysis not selected.

reported_success.quote: None of the studies provided any evidence that honesty priming increases candor of responding.

notes:
Original full primary paper unavailable: DOI landing not accessible; CiteSeer PDF returned 404/timeout; Unpaywall and OpenAlex report no open-access location. Original statistics quoted secondarily in replication paper were not used. Supplied replication page locators appear to refer to a manuscript rather than the six-page published article.
Source follow-up: Published article title and DOI match the assigned original reference. Extracted the omnibus alcohol-composite prime effect at the supplied p. 4 locator, rather than the separate order interaction, order-specific contrasts or individual alcohol items. The requested test statistic is printed as F; no metric conversion. Original only; replication and narrative replication success were not examined.
